headline: Brazil's grid operator has given 228 megawatts of grid capacity to three data center projects in São Paulo state.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 3: the award was made on 6 Oct 2026, so the pool item is a late repost, and the amount is small next to the demand.
importance_line: Data-center developers in Brazil now know grid access will be decided in competitive rounds, and demand far exceeds what is available, but 228 megawatts is small next to the more than 20 gigawatts requested.
summary: W.Media reports, citing a press release from Brazil's National Electric System Operator (ONS), that ONS awarded all 228 megawatts of remaining grid capacity at four connection points in São Paulo state to three data center projects, two on CloudHQ's GRU campus and one expanding NextStream's Tamboré campus, after seven projects with 451 megawatts of qualified demand competed. The first access round under Brazil's new transmission access policy drew 367 projects asking for more than 20 gigawatts nationwide; the award was made on 6 Oct 2026.
notes: Credit follows to W.Media (first outlet) citing the ONS release; ET Datacenters carried it on 10 Oct.
